# New renderings — iliad-156 (24.405–506)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν καὶ λισσόμενος Πρίαμος πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε (24.485, whole-line speech introduction) | "Him also, begging, Priam addressed with a word:" | "And Priam, begging, spoke to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "in turn" (reserved for αὖτε); λισσόμενος keeps "begging" (16.46); καί is a light particle and is kept as "also" in `l` only |
| ὣς φάτο, γήθησεν δ’ ὃ γέρων, καὶ ἀμείβετο μύθῳ (24.424, whole line) | "So he spoke, and the old man rejoiced, and answered with a word:" | "So he spoke, and the old man was glad, and answered him:" | follows the table's ὣς φάτο, κώκυσεν δὲ γυνὴ καὶ ἀμείβετο μύθῳ (24.200) and γήθησεν "rejoiced" |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπέβη πρὸς μακρὸν Ὄλυμπον Ἑρμείας (24.468–469) | "So then, having spoken, went away to tall Olympus / Hermes;" | "With these words Hermes went away to tall Olympus;" | follows the table's ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπεβήσετο (2.35) and μακρὸν Ὄλυμπον "tall Olympus" |
| ἄτη πυκινή (24.480) | "thick bewilderment" | "thick bewilderment" | "blind folly", "ruin"; keeps the table's ἄτη "bewilderment" (1.412); πυκινός "thick" |
| ὀλοῷ ἐπὶ γήραος οὐδῷ (24.487) | "on the baneful threshold of old age" | "on the baneful threshold of old age" | "deadly", "grim", "ruinous" (reserved for οὐλόμενος); ὀλοός keeps "baneful" (3.133; 24.39 ships "deadly" of a person) |
| ἀρὴν καὶ λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι (24.489) | "ward off harm and ruin" | "ward off harm and ruin" | "curse" (a later sense of ἀρή), "doom", "keep off" (the table’s ἀμῦναι is "ward off", 1.341); λοιγός "ruin" (1.341) |
| ὑπὸ γούνατ’ ἔλυσεν (24.498) | "loosed the knees" | "loosed the knees" | "killed", "brought low"; the table's 11.579 idiom kept whole |
| ἐριούνιος Ἑρμείας (24.440, 24.457) | "the helper" · "Hermes the helper" | "the helper" · "Hermes the helper" (+ note: meaning unknown, "helper" one ancient guess) | follows the table's ἐριούνιος "the helper" (24.360) |
| ὄζος Ἄρηος (Ἄλκιμος, 24.474) | "scion of Ares" | "scion of Ares" | follows the table's ὄζος Ἄρηος (2.540, 2.704) |
| θεοῖς ἐπιείκελ’ Ἀχιλλεῦ (24.486) | "resembling the gods, Achilles" | "you who are like the gods" | the table's 9.485 row ("like the gods"), with the `i` recast to fit the vocative |
| ἐνδυκέως (24.438, of an escort) | "kindly" | "kindly" | "carefully", "attentively"; follows the Odyssey's ἐνδυκέως "kindly" (10.65) |
| ἀγαπαζέμεν ἄντην (24.464) | "to welcome … face to face" | "to welcome … openly like this, face to face" | "love", "greet fondly"; ἀγαπάζω "welcome" (14.381 ἀμφαγαπάζω); ἄντην "face to face" (18.307) |
| ἐπιρρήσσεσκον (τρεῖς … Ἀχαιοί, 24.454; Ἀχιλεὺς … ἐπιρρήσσεσκε, 24.456) | "used to drive home" | "would drive home" | "bolt", "close"; iterative -σκ- kept as "used to" / "would" |
| λάβε γούνατα (24.465 imperative, 24.478 aorist) | "take hold of the knees" · "took … knees" | "take hold of the knees" · "took hold of Achilles’ knees" | "clasp"; follows the table's λάβε γούνων "took hold of his knees" (1.500) |
| λήθετ’ ἐνὶ μεγάροισι θεῶν οἳ Ὄλυμπον ἔχουσι (24.427) | "forgot in the halls the gods who hold Olympus" | "never forgot, in his halls, the gods who hold Olympus" | the table's Ὀλύμπια δώματ’ ἔχοντες is a different phrase; "who hold Olympus" is plain |
| ἐπιβλής · κληΐς (24.453, 24.455, of the door of Achilles’ courtyard) | "cross-bar" · "bolt" | "cross-bar" · "bolt" | "bar" (kept for ὀχεύς, 12.121), "bolt" for ἐπιβλής (kept for κληΐς, 12.456); ἐπιβλής is what is thrown across, a cross-bar |
